# v0.30.3: a hotfix for the summary head stored again after a same-length pass

v0.30.3 is a hotfix on v0.30.2. It stops LCM-X from storing its own summary head as an extra user row after a same-length compaction pass, and it keeps a copy already stored out of the prompt and out of compaction. It changes no setting and no schema, and it writes nothing new to the store. The [v0.30.2 notes](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/tag/v0.30.2) still apply, except where this page says otherwise.

## Fixed

- **A same-length compaction pass no longer makes the next ingest store the summary head again.** Some passes return a list of the same length: a stub-first exit, or a pass whose only leaf covers hidden rows. The host then stamps the rows it was handed. On the next ingest, v0.30.2 could compare the regenerated summary head with the old head's cached timestamp, treat the head as a new row, and store it again as an extra user row. v0.30.3 records exact digests of the user rows it emitted (summary, carrier and objective) for that pass, in memory only. The next ingest trusts a row that matches its digest byte for byte, whatever its timestamp. This holds with `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID` unset (the default) or `on`. With `off`, a host whose save stamps the emitted head with a timestamp, a row id and a new uid can still get the head stored again, as on v0.30.2 (see Known issues).
- **A copy already stored stays stored, out of the prompt and out of compaction.** A stored user row is treated as LCM-X's own head only when all three hold: every summary part verifies byte for byte against this session's summary nodes; it carries the existing `generated_unproven` relation; and any carrier remainder is already stored as an earlier user row. Such a row stays in the store unchanged. It is left out of prompt assembly and out of compaction input. If a leaf already covers such a copy, publication accepts it as v0.30.2 does.

## Known issues

- **A store on SQLite older than 3.51.3 can lose whole recent transactions.** With SQLite before 3.51.3, a store in WAL mode with several connections can lose whole recent transactions, through SQLite's own WAL-reset bug ([#1085](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1085); evidence in [#2330](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2330)). This is a storage-layer loss below LCM-X, and v0.30.3 does not change it. Check your SQLite with `python3 -c "import sqlite3; print(sqlite3.sqlite_version)"`. v0.30.4 adds a loud startup warning ([#3058](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3058)).
- **The transcript repair for replies lost before v0.30.2 is not in this release** ([#3022](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3022)). The v0.30.2 notes planned it for v0.30.3. It moved to the next train. Hermes's own transcript still holds those replies.
- **Recall can still return a stored copy of a summary head.** The recall tools (`lcm_grep`, `lcm_expand` and the rest) are not changed in this release. Their exclusion is planned for v0.30.4.
- **With `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=off`, the summary head can still be stored again** ([#3060](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3060)). If the host's save stamps the emitted head with a timestamp, a row id and a new uid, the digest this release records no longer matches, and the next ingest stores the head again exactly as v0.30.2 does. Nothing is lost. This was shown on a synthetic host, not in a real Hermes session. With the setting unset (the default) or `on`, the fix holds. A fix is planned for v0.30.4.
- **A new user message that repeats an earlier one word for word can be left out of one assembly path** ([#3061](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3061)). This is new in v0.30.3. The head-copy check proves a carrier's remainder by its text, not by which stored row it came from. So when a host saves a new user message in the same row as a summary head, and that message repeats an earlier user message word for word, the row is treated as a stored head copy. On a synthetic host the row is stored whole, as on v0.30.2, but store-backed assembly then leaves it out, where v0.30.2 keeps it. On a Hermes-shaped message list, compaction still covers it, as on v0.30.2. The row stays stored and can be read back by id. A fix is planned for v0.30.4, before recall starts using this check.
- **The head-copy check looks up stored content without an index** ([#3062](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3062)). Each lookup of a carrier's remainder walks the session's earlier rows, and the check also runs inside the publication write. Its cost on a large store has not been measured yet. v0.30.4 measures it and fixes it.
- **With `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=on`, a stub-first exit can return a summary together with the raw rows it covers** ([#3048](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3048)). This is v0.30.2 behaviour, and this release does not change it. A fix is planned for v0.30.4.
- **A tool call and its result can still be stored twice on the first ingest after a restart** ([#3026](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/3026)). This is the v0.30.2 item "This release can store a second copy of a tool call and its result", unchanged. Nothing is lost; recall can return them twice. LCM-X keeps the copy rather than risk dropping a row.
- **Four older issues stay open, and each is still treated as top priority until it is re-measured on v0.30.2 or resolved.** v0.30.3 changes none of them.
  - Restart copies, and passes that can stop freeing anything after a cold start ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)). The v0.30.1 notes said work on this was planned for v0.30.3. It is not in this release. It is being measured on v0.30.2 by 2026-11-24, and v0.30.4 will either carry the change or update this note.
  - A slow first ingest after a host change, with compaction stuck behind it ([#2818](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2818)). It was measured on v0.30.0 only, and is being re-timed on v0.30.2 by 2026-11-24.
  - Compaction that stops on the same row at every pass ([#1162](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1162)), reported on a v0.30.1 release candidate. Two later changes may cover it, and a rerun on v0.30.2 has been asked for. There is no workaround yet.
  - A store already stuck behind an old hidden-only leaf stays stuck ([#1141](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1141)), seen on v0.28.1. There is no known way to reach this state at the default settings. There is no in-place repair and no workaround yet.

## Upgrade and rollback

- **Upgrade.** No setting change, no schema change, and no new store write.
- **Rollback.** Take a SQLite-safe backup first (see `docs/operator-guide.md`). The rollback target is v0.30.2, by a plain swap of the build. After this build reads or compacts a store, v0.30.2 reads it exactly as it would have (rollback cells below). After a rollback, the v0.30.2 known issues apply again, including the stored head copy.

## Qualification

- L1 on rc1 (112e3035) carries to this tag (ruling T1-566); its results are added here before the tag.

This fix changes ingest and compaction on the turn path, so it ships on the careful lane as a disclosed hotfix (release decisions T1-533, T1-536, T1-542, T1-547, T1-548 and T1-549).
- Tests aimed at the mechanism, red on v0.30.2 and green here in both host-uid modes: `tests/invariants/test_stub_exit_head_restore.py` (on v0.30.2 the replay stores the summary head again) and `tests/invariants/test_hotfix_stored_summary_head.py` (on v0.30.2 a stored copy changes the prompt and enters compaction). `tests/invariants/test_hotfix_host_shaped_passes.py` runs host-shaped passes over a store that holds a copy: each pass stores a leaf, with no stall, and the result matches a twin store without the copy.
- Two paired cells against v0.30.2, in both uid modes:
  - `tests/compat/test_hotfix_session_switch.py`: after a same-length pass in one session, a switch to a second session (by rotation, and while the first pass's proof is pending), whose first ingest carries a row byte-equal to the first session's emitted head. The second session stores exactly what v0.30.2 stores. The test also checks that the recorded digest did match that row, so the case it guards was exercised.
  - `tests/compat/test_hotfix_paired_three_passes.py`: three passes over a store holding copies. Each pass publishes at least what v0.30.2 publishes, leaves a prompt no larger than v0.30.2's, and shows no hold, no refusal and no repeated stop.
- Rollback cells against v0.30.2 (f77d6ed9), both uid modes: `tests/compat/test_hotfix_head_copy_rollback.py` and `tests/compat/test_hotfix_head_copy_rollback_after_pass.py`. After this build reads a store, or compacts across a copy, the store is byte-identical to an untouched twin, and v0.30.2 gives identical output.
- CI on the fix's final commit: [run 45062816685](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/actions/runs/45062816685) passed on its second attempt. The first attempt failed once in an unrelated test: the session-end compare matrix, on a `table metadata already exists` setup error. The full test suite also passed locally on the candidate: two known flaky cases passed on rerun, and five failures were environment-only.
- Review: two independent reviewers, one Claude and one cross-model, with one fix round and two delta checks. The fix round removed a publication-conflict raise that could have stalled compaction.
- The live-session rows D9-D12 do not run for this release. Their producer has not merged, and the spec lets a disclosed hotfix ship without them.
- Two checks of the smoke stage (L1) did not run on rc1: the session switch while a compaction pass waits for its summary ([#2851](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2851)) and the ordinal planner in a packed session ([#2840](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2840)). Their instrument ships with the same unmerged producer. The owner waived both once, for this release only (release decision T1-549): the fix is small, it blocks a known path (a stored copy of the summary head being read back by the next compaction), and it does not touch the planner. The PR adds a session-switch test for this fix's own mechanism.
- Not proven: these are synthetic stores, not a real host session. The first live install is watched for 72 hours.
